pali.mn10:1.2: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kurūsu viharati kammāsadhammaṁ nāma kurūnaṁ nigamo.
pali.mn10:2.1: “Ekāyano ayaṁ, bhikkhave, maggo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā, sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya, dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya, ñāyassa adhigamāya, nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā.
pali.mn10:3.2: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
pali.mn10:3.3: vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
pali.mn10:3.4: citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
pali.mn10:3.5: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
pali.mn10:4.1: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati?
pali.mn10:4.2: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati, pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā, ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya, parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
pali.mn10:4.4: Dīghaṁ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṁ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṁ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṁ passasāmī’ti pajānāti,
pali.mn10:4.5: rassaṁ vā assasanto ‘rassaṁ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṁ vā passasanto ‘rassaṁ passasāmī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:4.7: ‘Passambhayaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.
pali.mn10:4.8: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dakkho bhamakāro vā bhamakārantevāsī vā dīghaṁ vā añchanto ‘dīghaṁ añchāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṁ vā añchanto ‘rassaṁ añchāmī’ti pajānāti;
pali.mn10:4.9: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dīghaṁ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṁ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṁ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṁ passasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṁ vā assasanto ‘rassaṁ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṁ vā passasanto ‘rassaṁ passasāmī’ti pajānāti;
pali.mn10:4.11: ‘passambhayaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.
pali.mn10:5.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati;
pali.mn10:5.2: samudayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati.
pali.mn10:5.3: ‘Atthi kāyo’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
pali.mn10:5.4: Evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:6.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gacchanto vā ‘gacchāmī’ti pajānāti, ṭhito vā ‘ṭhitomhī’ti pajānāti, nisinno vā ‘nisinnomhī’ti pajānāti, sayāno vā ‘sayānomhī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:6.2: Yathā yathā vā panassa kāyo paṇihito hoti tathā tathā naṁ pajānāti.
pali.mn10:7.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati;
pali.mn10:7.2: samudayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati.
pali.mn10:7.3: ‘Atthi kāyo’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
pali.mn10:7.4: Evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:8.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti.
pali.mn10:9.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati …pe…
pali.mn10:9.2: evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:10.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṁ uddhaṁ pādatalā, adho kesamatthakā, tacapariyantaṁ pūraṁ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhati:
pali.mn10:10.2: ‘atthi imasmiṁ kāye kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṁsaṁ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṁ vakkaṁ hadayaṁ yakanaṁ kilomakaṁ pihakaṁ papphāsaṁ antaṁ antaguṇaṁ udariyaṁ karīsaṁ pittaṁ semhaṁ pubbo lohitaṁ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttan’ti.
pali.mn10:10.3: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ubhatomukhā putoḷi pūrā nānāvihitassa dhaññassa, seyyathidaṁ—sālīnaṁ vīhīnaṁ muggānaṁ māsānaṁ tilānaṁ taṇḍulānaṁ. Tamenaṁ cakkhumā puriso muñcitvā paccavekkheyya: ‘ime sālī ime vīhī ime muggā ime māsā ime tilā ime taṇḍulā’ti.
pali.mn10:10.4: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṁ uddhaṁ pādatalā, adho kesamatthakā, tacapariyantaṁ pūraṁ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhati:
pali.mn10:11.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati …pe…
pali.mn10:11.2: evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:12.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṁ yathāṭhitaṁ yathāpaṇihitaṁ dhātuso paccavekkhati:
pali.mn10:12.2: ‘atthi imasmiṁ kāye pathavīdhātu āpodhātu tejodhātu vāyodhātū’ti.
pali.mn10:12.3: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dakkho goghātako vā goghātakantevāsī vā gāviṁ vadhitvā catumahāpathe bilaso vibhajitvā nisinno assa.
pali.mn10:12.4: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṁ yathāṭhitaṁ yathāpaṇihitaṁ dhātuso paccavekkhati:
pali.mn10:12.5: ‘atthi imasmiṁ kāye pathavīdhātu āpodhātu tejodhātu vāyodhātū’ti.
pali.mn10:13.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati …pe…
pali.mn10:13.2: evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:14.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu seyyathāpi passeyya sarīraṁ sivathikāya chaḍḍitaṁ ekāhamataṁ vā dvīhamataṁ vā tīhamataṁ vā uddhumātakaṁ vinīlakaṁ vipubbakajātaṁ.
pali.mn10:15.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati …pe…
pali.mn10:15.2: evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:16.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu seyyathāpi passeyya sarīraṁ sivathikāya chaḍḍitaṁ kākehi vā khajjamānaṁ kulalehi vā khajjamānaṁ gijjhehi vā khajjamānaṁ kaṅkehi vā khajjamānaṁ sunakhehi vā khajjamānaṁ byagghehi vā khajjamānaṁ dīpīhi vā khajjamānaṁ siṅgālehi vā khajjamānaṁ vividhehi vā pāṇakajātehi khajjamānaṁ.
pali.mn10:17.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati …pe…
pali.mn10:17.2: evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:18-23.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu seyyathāpi passeyya sarīraṁ sivathikāya chaḍḍitaṁ aṭṭhikasaṅkhalikaṁ samaṁsalohitaṁ nhārusambandhaṁ …pe…
pali.mn10:24.1: Aṭṭhikāni apagatasambandhāni disā vidisā vikkhittāni, aññena hatthaṭṭhikaṁ aññena pādaṭṭhikaṁ aññena gopphakaṭṭhikaṁ aññena jaṅghaṭṭhikaṁ aññena ūruṭṭhikaṁ aññena kaṭiṭṭhikaṁ aññena phāsukaṭṭhikaṁ aññena piṭṭhiṭṭhikaṁ aññena khandhaṭṭhikaṁ aññena gīvaṭṭhikaṁ aññena hanukaṭṭhikaṁ aññena dantaṭṭhikaṁ aññena sīsakaṭāhaṁ.
pali.mn10:25.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati …pe…
pali.mn10:25.2: evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:26-28.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu seyyathāpi passeyya sarīraṁ sivathikāya chaḍḍitaṁ, aṭṭhikāni setāni saṅkhavaṇṇapaṭibhāgāni …pe…
pali.mn10:31.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati;
pali.mn10:31.2: samudayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati.
pali.mn10:31.3: ‘Atthi kāyo’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
pali.mn10:31.4: Evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:32.1: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati?
pali.mn10:32.2: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sukhaṁ vā vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘sukhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:32.3: Dukkhaṁ vā vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘dukkhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:32.4: Adukkhamasukhaṁ vā vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘adukkhamasukhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:32.5: Sāmisaṁ vā sukhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘sāmisaṁ sukhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:32.6: Nirāmisaṁ vā sukhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘nirāmisaṁ sukhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:32.7: Sāmisaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘sāmisaṁ dukkhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:32.8: Nirāmisaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘nirāmisaṁ dukkhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:32.9: Sāmisaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘sāmisaṁ adukkhamasukhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:32.10: Nirāmisaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘nirāmisaṁ adukkhamasukhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:33.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati;
pali.mn10:33.2: samudayadhammānupassī vā vedanāsu viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā vedanāsu viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā vedanāsu viharati.
pali.mn10:33.3: ‘Atthi vedanā’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
pali.mn10:33.4: Evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:34.1: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu citte cittānupassī viharati?
pali.mn10:34.2: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ ‘sarāgaṁ cittan’ti pajānāti.
pali.mn10:35.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā citte cittānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā citte cittānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā citte cittānupassī viharati;
pali.mn10:35.2: samudayadhammānupassī vā cittasmiṁ viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā cittasmiṁ viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā cittasmiṁ viharati.
pali.mn10:35.3: ‘Atthi cittan’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
pali.mn10:35.4: Evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu citte cittānupassī viharati.
pali.mn10:36.1: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati?
pali.mn10:36.2: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati pañcasu nīvaraṇesu.
pali.mn10:36.3: Kathañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati pañcasu nīvaraṇesu?
pali.mn10:36.4: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ kāmacchandaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ kāmacchando’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ kāmacchandaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ kāmacchando’ti pajānāti; yathā ca anuppannassa kāmacchandassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa kāmacchandassa pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa kāmacchandassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:36.5: Santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ byāpādaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ byāpādo’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ byāpādaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ byāpādo’ti pajānāti; yathā ca anuppannassa byāpādassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa byāpādassa pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa byāpādassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:36.6: Santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ thinamiddhaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ thinamiddhan’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ thinamiddhaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ thinamiddhan’ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa thinamiddhassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa thinamiddhassa pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa thinamiddhassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:36.7: Santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ uddhaccakukkuccaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ uddhaccakukkuccan’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ uddhaccakukkuccaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ uddhaccakukkuccan’ti pajānāti; yathā ca anuppannassa uddhaccakukkuccassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa uddhaccakukkuccassa pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa uddhaccakukkuccassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:36.8: Santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ vicikicchaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ vicikicchā’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ vicikicchaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ vicikicchā’ti pajānāti; yathā ca anuppannāya vicikicchāya uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannāya vicikicchāya pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnāya vicikicchāya āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:37.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati;
pali.mn10:37.2: samudayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati.
pali.mn10:37.3: ‘Atthi dhammā’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
pali.mn10:37.4: Evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati pañcasu nīvaraṇesu.
pali.mn10:38.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu.
pali.mn10:38.2: Kathañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu?
pali.mn10:38.4: ‘iti rūpaṁ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo;
pali.mn10:38.5: iti vedanā, iti vedanāya samudayo, iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo;
pali.mn10:38.6: iti saññā, iti saññāya samudayo, iti saññāya atthaṅgamo;
pali.mn10:38.7: iti saṅkhārā, iti saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo, iti saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo;
pali.mn10:38.8: iti viññāṇaṁ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti;
pali.mn10:39.1: iti ajjhattaṁ vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati;
pali.mn10:39.2: samudayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati.
pali.mn10:39.3: ‘Atthi dhammā’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
pali.mn10:39.4: Evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu.
pali.mn10:40.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati chasu ajjhattikabāhiresu āyatanesu.
pali.mn10:40.2: Kathañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati chasu ajjhattikabāhiresu āyatanesu?
pali.mn10:40.3: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhuñca pajānāti, rūpe ca pajānāti, yañca tadubhayaṁ paṭicca uppajjati saṁyojanaṁ tañca pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa saṁyojanassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa saṁyojanassa pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa saṁyojanassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:40.4: Sotañca pajānāti, sadde ca pajānāti, yañca tadubhayaṁ paṭicca uppajjati saṁyojanaṁ tañca pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa saṁyojanassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa saṁyojanassa pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa saṁyojanassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:40.5: Ghānañca pajānāti, gandhe ca pajānāti, yañca tadubhayaṁ paṭicca uppajjati saṁyojanaṁ tañca pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa saṁyojanassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa saṁyojanassa pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa saṁyojanassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:40.6: Jivhañca pajānāti, rase ca pajānāti, yañca tadubhayaṁ paṭicca uppajjati saṁyojanaṁ tañca pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa saṁyojanassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa saṁyojanassa pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa saṁyojanassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:40.7: Kāyañca pajānāti, phoṭṭhabbe ca pajānāti, yañca tadubhayaṁ paṭicca uppajjati saṁyojanaṁ tañca pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa saṁyojanassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa saṁyojanassa pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa saṁyojanassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:40.8: Manañca pajānāti, dhamme ca pajānāti, yañca tadubhayaṁ paṭicca uppajjati saṁyojanaṁ tañca pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa saṁyojanassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa saṁyojanassa pahānaṁ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa saṁyojanassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:41.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati;
pali.mn10:41.2: samudayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati.
pali.mn10:41.3: ‘Atthi dhammā’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
pali.mn10:41.4: Evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati chasu ajjhattikabāhiresu āyatanesu.
pali.mn10:42.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati sattasu bojjhaṅgesu.
pali.mn10:42.2: Kathañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati sattasu bojjhaṅgesu?
pali.mn10:42.3: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ satisambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ satisambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ satisambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:42.4: Santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:42.5: Santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ vīriyasambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ vīriyasambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:42.6: Santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ pītisambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ pītisambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ pītisambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ pītisambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa pītisambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:42.7: Santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ passaddhisambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ passaddhisambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:42.8: Santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ samādhisambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ samādhisambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ samādhisambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ samādhisambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa samādhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:42.9: Santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo’ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti.
pali.mn10:43.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati;
pali.mn10:43.2: samudayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati.
pali.mn10:43.3: ‘Atthi dhammā’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
pali.mn10:43.4: Evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati sattasu bojjhaṅgesu.
pali.mn10:44.1: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati catūsu ariyasaccesu.
pali.mn10:44.2: Kathañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati catūsu ariyasaccesu?
pali.mn10:44.3: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
pali.mn10:45.1: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati;
pali.mn10:45.2: samudayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā dhammesu viharati.
pali.mn10:45.3: ‘Atthi dhammā’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
pali.mn10:45.4: Evampi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati catūsu ariyasaccesu.
pali.mn10:46.1: Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne evaṁ bhāveyya satta vassāni, tassa dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ
pali.mn10:46.2: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā; sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā.
pali.mn10:46.4: Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne evaṁ bhāveyya cha vassāni …pe…
pali.mn10:46.11: Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne evaṁ bhāveyya satta māsāni, tassa dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ
pali.mn10:46.12: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā; sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā.
pali.mn10:46.14: Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne evaṁ bhāveyya cha māsāni …pe…
pali.mn10:46.22: Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne evaṁ bhāveyya sattāhaṁ, tassa dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ
pali.mn10:46.23: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā sati vā upādisese anāgāmitāti.
pali.mn10:47.1: ‘Ekāyano ayaṁ, bhikkhave, maggo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya yadidaṁ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’ti.
pali.mn10:47.2: Iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttan”ti.
pali.mn10:47.4: Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.

translation.mn10:1.2: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kurus, near the Kuru town named Kammāsadamma.
translation.mn10:1.3: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
translation.mn10:2.1: “Mendicants, the four kinds of mindfulness meditation are the path to convergence. They are in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to discover the system, and to realize extinguishment.
translation.mn10:3.2: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
translation.mn10:3.3: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
translation.mn10:3.4: They meditate observing an aspect of the mind—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
translation.mn10:3.5: They meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
translation.mn10:4.1: And how does a mendicant meditate observing an aspect of the body?
translation.mn10:4.2: It’s when a mendicant—gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut—sits down cross-legged, sets their body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.
translation.mn10:4.3: Just mindful, they breathe in. Mindful, they breathe out.
translation.mn10:4.4: Breathing in heavily they know: ‘I’m breathing in heavily.’ Breathing out heavily they know: ‘I’m breathing out heavily.’
translation.mn10:4.5: When breathing in lightly they know: ‘I’m breathing in lightly.’ Breathing out lightly they know: ‘I’m breathing out lightly.’
translation.mn10:4.6: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing the whole body.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing the whole body.’
translation.mn10:4.7: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in stilling the physical process.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out stilling the physical process.’
translation.mn10:4.8: It’s like a deft carpenter or carpenter’s apprentice. When making a deep cut they know: ‘I’m making a deep cut,’ and when making a shallow cut they know: ‘I’m making a shallow cut.’
translation.mn10:5.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of the body internally, externally, and both internally and externally.
translation.mn10:5.2: They meditate observing , with respect to the body, the liability to originate, to vanish, and to originate and vanish.
translation.mn10:5.3: Or mindfulness is established that the body exists, to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. They meditate independent, not grasping at anything in the world.
translation.mn10:5.4: That’s how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body.
translation.mn10:6.1: Furthermore, when a mendicant is walking they know: ‘I am walking.’ When standing they know: ‘I am standing.’ When sitting they know: ‘I am sitting.’ And when lying down they know: ‘I am lying down.’
translation.mn10:6.2: Whatever posture their body is in, they know it.
translation.mn10:7.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of the body internally, externally, and both internally and externally.
translation.mn10:7.2: With respect to the body, they meditate observing the liability to originate, to vanish, and to originate and vanish.
translation.mn10:7.3: Or mindfulness is established that the body exists, to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. They meditate independent, not grasping at anything in the world.
translation.mn10:7.4: That too is how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body.
translation.mn10:8.1: Furthermore, a mendicant acts with situational awareness when going out and coming back; when looking ahead and aside; when bending and extending the limbs; when bearing the outer robe, bowl and robes; when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; when urinating and defecating; when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent.
translation.mn10:9.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of the body internally …
translation.mn10:9.2: That too is how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body.
translation.mn10:10.1: Furthermore, a mendicant examines their own body, up from the soles of the feet and down from the tips of the hairs, wrapped in skin and full of many kinds of filth.
translation.mn10:10.2: ‘In this body there is head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, diaphragm, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, urine.’
translation.mn10:10.3: It’s as if there were a bag with openings at both ends, filled with various kinds of grains, such as fine rice, wheat, mung beans, peas, sesame, and ordinary rice. And a person with clear eyes were to open it and examine the contents: ‘These grains are fine rice, these are wheat, these are mung beans, these are peas, these are sesame, and these are ordinary rice.’
translation.mn10:11.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of the body internally …
translation.mn10:11.2: That too is how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body.
translation.mn10:12.1: Furthermore, a mendicant examines their own body, whatever its placement or posture, according to the elements:
translation.mn10:12.2: ‘In this body there is the earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the air element.’
translation.mn10:12.3: It’s as if a deft butcher or butcher’s apprentice were to kill a cow and sit down at the crossroads with the meat cut into chops.
translation.mn10:13.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of the body internally …
translation.mn10:13.2: That too is how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body.
translation.mn10:14.1: Furthermore, suppose a mendicant were to see a corpse discarded in a charnel ground. And it had been dead for one, two, or three days, bloated, livid, and festering.
translation.mn10:14.2: They’d compare it with their own body:
translation.mn10:14.3: ‘This body is also of that same nature, that same kind, and cannot go beyond that.’
translation.mn10:15.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of the body internally …
translation.mn10:15.2: That too is how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body.
translation.mn10:16.1: Furthermore, suppose they were to see a corpse discarded in a charnel ground being devoured by crows, hawks, vultures, herons, hounds, tigers, leopards, jackals, and many kinds of little creatures.
translation.mn10:16.2: They’d compare it with their own body:
translation.mn10:16.3: ‘This body is also of that same nature, that same kind, and cannot go beyond that.’
translation.mn10:17.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of the body internally …
translation.mn10:17.2: That too is how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body.
translation.mn10:18-23.1: Furthermore, suppose they were to see a corpse discarded in a charnel ground, a skeleton with flesh and blood, held together by sinews …
translation.mn10:18-23.2: A skeleton without flesh but smeared with blood, and held together by sinews …
translation.mn10:18-23.3: A skeleton rid of flesh and blood, held together by sinews …
translation.mn10:24.1: Bones rid of sinews scattered in every direction. Here a hand-bone, there a foot-bone, here an ankle bone, there a shin-bone, here a thigh-bone, there a hip-bone, here a rib-bone, there a back-bone, here an arm-bone, there a neck-bone, here a jaw-bone, there a tooth, here the skull. …
translation.mn10:26-28.1: White bones, the color of shells …
translation.mn10:29.1: Decrepit bones, heaped in a pile …
translation.mn10:30.1: Bones rotted and crumbled to powder.
translation.mn10:30.2: They’d compare it with their own body:
translation.mn10:30.3: ‘This body is also of that same nature, that same kind, and cannot go beyond that.’
translation.mn10:31.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of the body internally, externally, and both internally and externally.
translation.mn10:31.2: With respect to the body, they meditate observing the liability to originate, to vanish, and to originate and vanish.
translation.mn10:31.3: Or mindfulness is established that the body exists, to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. They meditate independent, not grasping at anything in the world.
translation.mn10:31.4: That too is how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body.
translation.mn10:32.1: And how does a mendicant meditate observing an aspect of feelings?
translation.mn10:32.2: It’s when a mendicant who feels a pleasant feeling knows: ‘I feel a pleasant feeling.’
translation.mn10:32.3: When they feel a painful feeling, they know: ‘I feel a painful feeling.’
translation.mn10:32.4: When they feel a neutral feeling, they know: ‘I feel a neutral feeling.’
translation.mn10:32.5: When they feel a pleasant feeling of the flesh, they know: ‘I feel a pleasant feeling of the flesh.’
translation.mn10:32.6: When they feel a pleasant feeling not of the flesh, they know: ‘I feel a pleasant feeling not of the flesh.’
translation.mn10:32.7: When they feel a painful feeling of the flesh, they know: ‘I feel a painful feeling of the flesh.’
translation.mn10:32.8: When they feel a painful feeling not of the flesh, they know: ‘I feel a painful feeling not of the flesh.’
translation.mn10:32.9: When they feel a neutral feeling of the flesh, they know: ‘I feel a neutral feeling of the flesh.’
translation.mn10:32.10: When they feel a neutral feeling not of the flesh, they know: ‘I feel a neutral feeling not of the flesh.’
translation.mn10:33.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of feelings internally, externally, and both internally and externally.
translation.mn10:33.2: With respect to feelings, they meditate observing the liability to originate, to vanish, and to originate and vanish.
translation.mn10:33.3: Or mindfulness is established that feelings exist, to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. They meditate independent, not grasping at anything in the world.
translation.mn10:33.4: That’s how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of feelings.
translation.mn10:34.1: And how does a mendicant meditate observing an aspect of the mind?
translation.mn10:34.2: It’s when a mendicant understands mind with greed as ‘mind with greed,’
translation.mn10:34.3: and mind without greed as ‘mind without greed.’
translation.mn10:34.4: They understand mind with hate as ‘mind with hate,’
translation.mn10:34.5: and mind without hate as ‘mind without hate.’
translation.mn10:34.6: They understand mind with delusion as ‘mind with delusion,’
translation.mn10:34.7: and mind without delusion as ‘mind without delusion.’
translation.mn10:34.8: They know constricted mind as ‘constricted mind,’
translation.mn10:34.10: They know expansive mind as ‘expansive mind,’
translation.mn10:34.12: They know mind that is not supreme as ‘mind that is not supreme,’
translation.mn10:34.13: and mind that is supreme as ‘mind that is supreme.’
translation.mn10:34.14: They know mind immersed in samādhi as ‘mind immersed in samādhi,’
translation.mn10:34.15: and mind not immersed in samādhi as ‘mind not immersed in samādhi.’
translation.mn10:34.16: They know freed mind as ‘freed mind,’
translation.mn10:35.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of the mind internally, externally, and both internally and externally.
translation.mn10:35.2: With respect to the mind, they meditate observing the liability to originate, to vanish, and to originate and vanish.
translation.mn10:35.3: Or mindfulness is established that the mind exists, to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. They meditate independent, not grasping at anything in the world.
translation.mn10:35.4: That’s how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the mind.
translation.mn10:36.1: And how does a mendicant meditate observing an aspect of principles?
translation.mn10:36.2: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles with respect to the five hindrances.
translation.mn10:36.3: And how does a mendicant meditate observing an aspect of principles with respect to the five hindrances?
translation.mn10:36.4: It’s when a mendicant who has sensual desire in them understands: ‘I have sensual desire in me.’ When they don’t have sensual desire in them, they understand: ‘I don’t have sensual desire in me.’ They understand how sensual desire arises; how, when it’s already arisen, it’s given up; and how, once it’s given up, it doesn’t arise again in the future.
translation.mn10:36.5: When they have ill will in them, they understand: ‘I have ill will in me.’ When they don’t have ill will in them, they understand: ‘I don’t have ill will in me.’ They understand how ill will arises; how, when it’s already arisen, it’s given up; and how, once it’s given up, it doesn’t arise again in the future.
translation.mn10:36.6: When they have dullness and drowsiness in them, they understand: ‘I have dullness and drowsiness in me.’ When they don’t have dullness and drowsiness in them, they understand: ‘I don’t have dullness and drowsiness in me.’ They understand how dullness and drowsiness arise; how, when they’ve already arisen, they’re given up; and how, once they’re given up, they don’t arise again in the future.
translation.mn10:36.7: When they have restlessness and remorse in them, they understand: ‘I have restlessness and remorse in me.’ When they don’t have restlessness and remorse in them, they understand: ‘I don’t have restlessness and remorse in me.’ They understand how restlessness and remorse arise; how, when they’ve already arisen, they’re given up; and how, once they’re given up, they don’t arise again in the future.
translation.mn10:36.8: When they have doubt in them, they understand: ‘I have doubt in me.’ When they don’t have doubt in them, they understand: ‘I don’t have doubt in me.’ They understand how doubt arises; how, when it’s already arisen, it’s given up; and how, once it’s given up, it doesn’t arise again in the future.
translation.mn10:37.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of principles internally, externally, and both internally and externally.
translation.mn10:37.2: They meditate observing, with respect to the principles, the liability to originate, to vanish, and to originate and vanish.
translation.mn10:37.3: Or mindfulness is established that principles exist, to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. They meditate independent, not grasping at anything in the world.
translation.mn10:37.4: That’s how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles with respect to the five hindrances.
translation.mn10:38.1: Furthermore, a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles with respect to the five grasping aggregates.
translation.mn10:38.2: And how does a mendicant meditate observing an aspect of principles with respect to the five grasping aggregates?
translation.mn10:38.4: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form.
translation.mn10:38.5: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the ending of feeling.
translation.mn10:38.6: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the ending of perception.
translation.mn10:38.7: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the ending of choices.
translation.mn10:38.8: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the ending of consciousness.’
translation.mn10:39.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of principles internally …
translation.mn10:39.4: That’s how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles with respect to the five grasping aggregates.
translation.mn10:40.1: Furthermore, a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles with respect to the six interior and exterior sense fields.
translation.mn10:40.2: And how does a mendicant meditate observing an aspect of principles with respect to the six interior and exterior sense fields?
translation.mn10:40.3: It’s when a mendicant understands the eye, sights, and the fetter that arises dependent on both of these. They understand how the fetter that has not arisen comes to arise; how the arisen fetter comes to be abandoned; and how the abandoned fetter comes to not rise again in the future.
translation.mn10:40.4: They understand the ear, sounds, and the fetter …
translation.mn10:40.5: They understand the nose, smells, and the fetter …
translation.mn10:40.6: They understand the tongue, tastes, and the fetter …
translation.mn10:40.7: They understand the body, touches, and the fetter …
translation.mn10:40.8: They understand the mind, ideas, and the fetter that arises dependent on both of these. They understand how the fetter that has not arisen comes to arise; how the arisen fetter comes to be abandoned; and how the abandoned fetter comes to not rise again in the future.
translation.mn10:41.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of principles internally …
translation.mn10:41.4: That’s how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles with respect to the six interior and exterior sense fields.
translation.mn10:42.1: Furthermore, a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles with respect to the seven awakening factors.
translation.mn10:42.2: And how does a mendicant meditate observing an aspect of principles with respect to the seven awakening factors?
translation.mn10:42.3: It’s when a mendicant who has the awakening factor of mindfulness in them understands: ‘I have the awakening factor of mindfulness in me.’ When they don’t have the awakening factor of mindfulness in them, they understand: ‘I don’t have the awakening factor of mindfulness in me.’ They understand how the awakening factor of mindfulness that has not arisen comes to arise; and how the awakening factor of mindfulness that has arisen becomes fulfilled by development.
translation.mn10:42.4: When they have the awakening factor of investigation of principles …
translation.mn10:42.9: equanimity in them, they understand: ‘I have the awakening factor of equanimity in me.’ When they don’t have the awakening factor of equanimity in them, they understand: ‘I don’t have the awakening factor of equanimity in me.’ They understand how the awakening factor of equanimity that has not arisen comes to arise; and how the awakening factor of equanimity that has arisen becomes fulfilled by development.
translation.mn10:43.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of principles internally, externally, and both internally and externally.
translation.mn10:43.2: They meditate observing, with respect to the principles, the liability to originate, to vanish, and to originate and vanish.
translation.mn10:43.3: Or mindfulness is established that principles exist, to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. They meditate independent, not grasping at anything in the world.
translation.mn10:43.4: That’s how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles with respect to the seven awakening factors.
translation.mn10:44.1: Furthermore, a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles with respect to the four noble truths.
translation.mn10:44.2: And how does a mendicant meditate observing an aspect of principles with respect to the four noble truths?
translation.mn10:44.3: It’s when a mendicant truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.’
translation.mn10:45.1: And so they meditate observing an aspect of principles internally, externally, and both internally and externally.
translation.mn10:45.2: They meditate observing, with respect to the principles, the liability to originate, to vanish, and to originate and vanish.
translation.mn10:45.3: Or mindfulness is established that principles exist, to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. They meditate independent, not grasping at anything in the world.
translation.mn10:45.4: That’s how a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles with respect to the four noble truths.
translation.mn10:46.1: Anyone who develops these four kinds of mindfulness meditation in this way for seven years can expect one of two results:
translation.mn10:46.2: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.
translation.mn10:46.4: anyone who develops these four kinds of mindfulness meditation in this way for six years …
translation.mn10:46.22: anyone who develops these four kinds of mindfulness meditation in this way for seven days can expect one of two results:
translation.mn10:46.23: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.
translation.mn10:47.1: ‘The four kinds of mindfulness meditation are the path to convergence. They are in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to discover the system, and to realize extinguishment.’
translation.mn10:47.2: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”
translation.mn10:47.3: That is what the Buddha said.
translation.mn10:47.4: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.
